messages:
sarah: FYI — scheduling a staged drain in eu-west5 tonight 00:30-02:30 UTC to replace the backplane firmware on a subset of mixed-GPU racks (A100 + H100). Will do cohort-by-cohort, aim is 2 racks at a time. Need coordination on routing, kv-cache reseed, and tenant routing. :spiral_calendar:

alex: ack. what's the planned cohort size and drain order? any reserved capacity?

sarah: Cohorts = 2 racks (approx 48 GPUs). Order: thermal-high first (to avoid hot-swap backpressure), then mixed-density. Reserved capacity: we have ~10% burst headroom in us-west and eu-central that we can route to, but eu-west remains tight. We'll run graceful canaries before each cohort.

priyanka: can we route dedicated tenants to dedicated pools in another region? cc @tim for SLO impact and comms.

tim: For enterprise tenants on Dedicated we can failover to eu-central for critical traffic, but that increases egress cost and token latency by ~80-120ms. I recommend only routing critical tenants; non-critical hosted traffic should hit cheaper fallback models in-region.

alex: cost tradeoff noted. do we have capacity calc? how many requests/sec can we absorb if 2 racks out?

sarah: Quick estimate: removing cohort reduces peak throughput by ~18%. With KV cache hit rates at 68% we can absorb ~12% with autoscale; remaining ~6% will either queue or hit fallback. Plan: enable routing policy `egress:fallback-lane` to spill non-SLA traffic to smaller instances.

priyanka: schedule for the canary? also need to pre-seed KV cache after rollback windows.

sarah: Canary per cohort: 10m warmup, run 5% production traffic, run perf checks (tail latency, 95th), then proceed. KV reseed: after each cohort completes we'll run kv-seed job to prefill common prefixes for chat workloads.

tim: define perf checks please. I want a pass/fail so ops can abort quickly.

alex: propose checks: 95th latency < 250ms (generation), error rate < 0.3%, throughput within 90% baseline. If any fail -> rollback and mark cohort as degraded.

sarah: agreed. We'll also watch disk i/o and thermal sensors during power cycle. Oncall will have authority to abort.

oncall-bot: Reminder: nightly-maint window set in PagerDuty to 00:15-03:00 UTC for eu-west5. On-call is: tim.

deploy-bot: Deploy plan created: `playbooks/ops/eu-west5-backplane/7990012346-plan` (links: https://confluence.redwood/ops/eu-west5-backplane).

alex: any special driver/firmware differences between A100/H100 that require different node images?

sarah: A100 nodes are on driver 525.x, H100 on 535.x. New backplane firmware requires a micro-reboot sequence that temporarily hides GPUs from the OS for ~30s. That's why we do 2-rack cohorts and stagger pod eviction to avoid cold-cache stampedes.

priyanka: eviction plan? do not drain all GPU nodes at once obviously. We'll use `kubectl drain` with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60` and our custom pre-stop hook to flush KV entries. Sample command:

```
# drain example
kubectl drain gpu-node-xyz --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60 --timeout=5m
```

sarah: exact drain will be automated via runbook: `opsctl drain-cohort --cohort 3 --stagger 30s` which drains one node, waits 30s, then next. This staggers eviction to keep the frontends from hitting cold-cache simultaneously.

tim: please ensure autoscaler target is bumped before drain starts. Alex, can infra increase target from 1.2x -> 1.4x for window?

alex: I can up the target 30m before start and have it revert 15m after. Will annotate the policy with reason `eu-west5-backplane-maint`.

priyanka: customer comms? We should notify customers with heavy usage in eu-west5 about elevated latencies and potential cross-region routing. Draft: short email + console banner for 00:15-03:00 UTC, include fallbacks and expected latency uplift.

tim: yes. Also include contact path for critical SLA reclaim (we'll keep a 2-hr support hotline).

sarah: Ops checklist (short):
- bump autoscaler 30m prior
- run canary with 5% traffic per cohort
- monitor 95th latency, error rate, thermal metrics
- kv-seed after cohort complete
- rollback if checks fail
- run post-maint health-checks and revert autoscaler

alex: adding netpol egress throttle test after cohort 2 to validate our fallback lanes. That is: simulate 20% egress shaping for 5m to see how routing holds.

sarah: Good. That test will be after cohort 2 completion. If it degrades, we'll pause further cohorts.

priyanka: timeline summary:
00:00 - prep + bump autoscaler
00:30 - cohort 1 canary + warmup (10m)
00:50 - cohort 1 full drain + kv-seed (20-30m)
01:30 - cohort 2 canary + warmup
01:50 - cohort 2 full drain + kv-seed + egress-throttle-test
02:30 - wrap, post-checks, revert autoscaler

tim: lgtm. please post final comms to #customer-status and update runbook. I'll be oncall and standing by. :thumbsup:

sarah: thanks — I'll post the comms now and kick off the playbook at 23:55 UTC for prechecks. If anyone wants to join the run, ping me.

alex: I'll handle autoscaler bump and netpol test orchestration.

priyanka: I'll prepare the customer banner and escalation doc.

deploy-bot: Playbook executed at 23:55 UTC: preflight checks passed.

sarah: closing loop — all set. Will update thread with live cohort start pings. :wave:
